alerts.barrier_evidence: REAL PRE-ACCESS NAME FILTER at role.py:327: parts are dropped unless `part != '..' and '~' not in part and '$' not in part`, and the name is rebuilt via join(*final_parts) before extraction. For the FLAGGED data component (member.name) this blocks '..'-segment traversal on posix (absolute names lose their leading '/' as a split artifact; '~'/'$' parts dropped). It is a blacklist, not a root-containment check, and known residuals exist: (a) symlink members (member.issym(), :323) are extracted with UNFILTERED member.linkname — a symlink whose name passes the filter but whose linkname points outside gives a second-order traversal for subsequent file members; (b) only os.sep is split — alternate separators survive on non-posix controllers; (c) join(*[]) degenerates to ''. None of these residual vectors is the data flow that was flagged (the flagged flow is the name, which is filtered).
alerts.attacker_control_preconditions: for the flagged flow: a malicious galaxy role tar whose member NAME contains '..' — blocked by the filter; for the residual vectors: crafted symlink member linknames (not flagged)
alerts.impact: via the flagged flow: contained within roles_path; via unfiltered linkname: potential arbitrary file overwrite during role install
alerts.rationale: sink and taint are real, but the specific tainted component (rebuilt member.name) passes through a genuine '..'/'~'/'$' filter before extraction — the alert fired because the query does not model this filter as a barrier. The genuinely dangerous residual (symlink linkname, alternate separators) is outside the flagged path, so the alert as stated overstates the name-based risk while pointing at a function with real residual weaknesses.

cross_cutting_findings.protection_misclassification_risk: None of the reviewed alerts treats normpath/realpath/unfrackpath/login-auth alone as protection — the query correctly models them as propagators. The genuine protections found in the tree that DO justify FP verdicts are: module_loader membership checks (package.py:60, service.py:60), the galaxy role part filter (role.py:327), and basename in the fetch flat branch / fileglob / filetree term handling.
cross_cutting_findings.decoding_and_separator_factors: percent-decoding of lookup terms happens at dataloader.py:178 (unquote) — single decode, no re-decode loop found; fetch.py:106-107 applies shell unquote + backslash->slash normalization which preserves '..' segments; dataloader.py:181/:222/:283 absolute-path passthrough is the dominant escape primitive on every lookup chain.
cross_cutting_findings.async_wrapper_gaps: no interprocedural edge in the reviewed flows depended on an unproven async hop; all hops are direct calls or returns (e.g. _execute_module -> _parse_returned_data -> return data at action/__init__.py:982 -> fetch.py:83).
cross_cutting_findings.main_fp_root_causes: (1) tuple pack/unpack taint spreading element-to-element (module_data -> module_path, alerts #1-#3 flows 2-4, #19-#22 tuple returns); (2) oracle-grade sinks counted at full severity (os.stat/lstat/readlink/glob/walk); (3) operator-trust inventory variables rendered as sources (inventory_hostname); (4) remote-side path arguments flagged as controller sinks (fetch_file arg 0).

No source was labeled in collection.py: neither file_info['name'] (subscript at :180) nor the json.loads at :174 (RemoteResultLoads covers only 8 json.loads sites in winrm/psrp/network_cli/task_executor/interpreter_discovery/action __init__), and the tar member iteration loop itself was not treated as a boundary.

why_missed.notes: the nearest formal alert is #35 at galaxy/role.py:330 (role install extract), which is a DIFFERENT function and a different chain — role install with its own pre-access name filter, not the collection-install chain fixed by commit b2551bb.

pyvul_vulnerability_match_check.verdict: MISS — the real, present, exploitable path traversal fixed by CVE-2020-10691 (collection tar install, _extract_tar_file) was NOT captured by the pass-1 formal result set. Root cause is a source-modeling coverage gap (galaxy collection tar member/FILES.json names not labeled as sources), not a sink or propagation gap.

overall_conclusion: CodeQL analysis succeeded and produced 37 formal pass1 path-traversal alerts; after independent path review: 18 likely_tp (fetch dest chain, win_copy query-return chain, lookup file/template/password chains — all with explicitly stated attacker preconditions), 15 likely_fp, 4 uncertain. The project's one real known-style vulnerability in this tree (CVE-2020-10691, galaxy collection _extract_tar_file) was NOT among the hits due to a source-coverage gap in collection.py. No diagnostics, built-in query results, or non-CWE-22 findings were mixed into the formal result set.
